links.outcome: VLM-generated CXR report quality versus radiologist-written reports on same cases
links.effect: AIRead had lower RADPEER 3b rate (5.3% vs 13.9%) and higher acceptability (84.5% vs 74.3%) than radiologists; other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%) and lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%).
links.quote: Other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%; p < 0.05), lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%; p < 0.05), and more frequent hallucinations (5.4-17.4%; p < 0.05).

links.outcome: Hallucination rates in AI-generated chest radiograph reports
links.effect: AIRead hallucination 0.3% (4/1425) vs radiologists 0.1% (1/1425), p=0.21; other VLMs had hallucination rates of 5.4-17.4%.
links.quote: Other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%; p < 0.05), lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%; p < 0.05), and more frequent hallucinations (5.4-17.4%; p < 0.05).

screen.reason: Retrospective comparative evaluation and reader study benchmarking five vision-language models against radiologist reports without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
